tfResources.role: Primary/direct equivalent. Covers nearly all top-level scalar props 1:1 (with some renames — see attributeNotes; note autoScalingGroupName -> name) and most nested structs as native nested blocks: availability_zone_distribution, capacity_reservation_specification (+ capacity_reservation_target), instance_maintenance_policy, launch_template, mixed_instances_policy (instances_distribution + launch_template{launch_template_specification, override[]{instance_requirements...}}), initial_lifecycle_hook[] (from LifecycleHookSpecificationList), tag[] (from Tags), traffic_source[] (from TrafficSources), warm_pool (note: Cfn models warm pool as the separate AWS::AutoScaling::WarmPool resource, not part of CfnAutoScalingGroupProps).

Required companion resource for NotificationConfiguration (deprecated singular) / NotificationConfigurations (array). aws_autoscaling_group has NO inline notification block, so every {TopicArn, NotificationTypes} entry must be lifted out into a standalone aws_autoscaling_notification (group_names: [asg.name], notifications: NotificationTypes, topic_arn: TopicArn). Since TF's group_names/notifications are top-level lists (not per-topic), CFN's array of NotificationConfigurationProperty items typically collapses into one aws_autoscaling_notification per distinct topic_arn.

Referenced only, not created from this resource. LaunchTemplate.LaunchTemplateSpecification / MixedInstancesPolicy...LaunchTemplateSpecification / LaunchTemplateOverrides.LaunchTemplateSpecification all point to an id/name of a pre-existing launch template (separate AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate Cfn resource, mapped separately).
Referenced only. LaunchConfigurationName (string | ILaunchConfigurationRef) points to a pre-existing launch configuration (deprecated path); not created by this resource's props.

Optional alternative to the inline initial_lifecycle_hook block on aws_autoscaling_group. Same fields as LifecycleHookSpecificationProperty (default_result, heartbeat_timeout, lifecycle_transition, name/lifecycle_hook_name, notification_metadata, notification_target_arn, role_arn). Prefer inline initial_lifecycle_hook for a straight port of LifecycleHookSpecificationList; use this standalone resource only if hooks need to be added/removed independently of the ASG.

Optional/legacy alternative to the inline load_balancers / target_group_arns attributes on aws_autoscaling_group for LoadBalancerNames / TargetGroupArns. Prefer the inline attributes for a direct port.
Optional alternative to the inline traffic_source block for TrafficSources (TrafficSourceIdentifierProperty). Prefer inline traffic_source for a direct port.
Optional alternative to the inline tag block for Tags (TagPropertyProperty). Prefer inline tag[] for a direct port; use this only for out-of-band/per-tag management of an existing ASG.

attributeNotes:
Props with NO direct TF attribute on aws_autoscaling_group (drop / handle out-of-band):
- AvailabilityZoneImpairmentPolicy {ImpairedZoneHealthCheckBehavior, ZonalShiftEnabled} — no equivalent field anywhere in aws_autoscaling_group's schema (checked full Config interface; confirmed absent in provider 6.52.0). Newer Cfn-only ASG zonal-shift-impairment feature; no TF surface.
- InstanceLifecyclePolicy — entire struct has no TF equivalent. Its only member is RetentionTriggers.TerminateHookAbandon (string); drop or flag the whole block as unsupported.
- SkipZonalShiftValidation — no TF equivalent found (TF has no matching boolean); drop or flag as unsupported.
- InstanceId (legacy "create ASG from a running instance" Cfn feature) — no TF equivalent (TF ASGs are always created via launch_configuration/launch_template/mixed_instances_policy); flag as unsupported migration path.
- AutoScalingGroupARN (cloudformationAttribute) — becomes the TF computed attribute `arn` on aws_autoscaling_group (name differs: AutoScalingGroupARN -> arn).

Renames (same semantics, different TF field name):
- AutoScalingGroupName -> name (TF also exposes name_prefix as a TF-only alternative; leave unset when porting an explicit name).
- Cooldown -> default_cooldown
- NewInstancesProtectedFromScaleIn -> protect_from_scale_in
- LoadBalancerNames -> load_balancers
- MetricsCollection (array of {Granularity, Metrics[]}) -> flattens to two separate top-level TF attributes: metrics_granularity (string) + enabled_metrics (string[]). Shape mismatch: Cfn nests granularity+metrics per collection entry (and allows the array form), TF only supports one granularity value for all enabled metrics — collapse multiple MetricsCollection entries by taking a single Granularity (must be "1Minute" either way) and unioning Metrics into enabled_metrics.
- LaunchConfigurationName -> launch_configuration (Cfn typed as string | ILaunchConfigurationRef; TF is plain string — cross-stack refs resolve to the plain name string).

Clean 1:1 top-level scalars (snake_case only, no rename/reshape): availabilityZones->availability_zones, capacityRebalance->capacity_rebalance, context->context, desiredCapacityType->desired_capacity_type, healthCheckGracePeriod->health_check_grace_period, healthCheckType->health_check_type, maxInstanceLifetime->max_instance_lifetime, placementGroup->placement_group, serviceLinkedRoleArn->service_linked_role_arn, terminationPolicies->termination_policies, vpcZoneIdentifier->vpc_zone_identifier, defaultInstanceWarmup->default_instance_warmup.

Type/shape mismatches:
- MaxSize, MinSize, DesiredCapacity are `string` in Cfn (CloudFormation-generated legacy quirk) but `number` in TF (max_size: number [required], min_size: number [required], desired_capacity?: number) — must coerce string->number.
- Tags (Cfn: `Array<TagPropertyProperty>` with required Key/Value/PropagateAtLaunch) maps cleanly 1:1 in shape to TF `tag[]` {key, value, propagate_at_launch} — same field names once casing is snake_cased, no restructuring needed.
- TrafficSources (Cfn TrafficSourceIdentifierProperty {Identifier, Type}) maps 1:1 to TF traffic_source[] {identifier, type} — clean (note: Cfn's Type is required/non-optional here; TF type is optional).
- LifecycleHookSpecificationList items map 1:1 to TF initial_lifecycle_hook[] fields (defaultResult->default_result, heartbeatTimeout->heartbeat_timeout, lifecycleHookName->name [required in TF], lifecycleTransition->lifecycle_transition [required in TF], notificationMetadata->notification_metadata, notificationTargetArn->notification_target_arn, roleArn->role_arn) — clean; TF's initial_lifecycle_hook is applied only on ASG *creation* (changes require replacement/other tooling), matching Cfn's "specification list at creation time" semantics.
- MixedInstancesPolicy nests identically in both: InstancesDistribution / LaunchTemplate{LaunchTemplateSpecification, Overrides[]} / InstanceRequirements(...) <-> instances_distribution / launch_template{launch_template_specification, override[]} / instance_requirements(...) — deep structural parity confirmed (accelerator_count, accelerator_total_memory_mib, baseline_ebs_bandwidth_mbps, memory_gib_per_vcpu, memory_mib, network_bandwidth_gbps, network_interface_count, total_local_storage_gb, vcpu_count all present as matching nested Min/Max range objects on both sides).
- CapacityReservationSpecification{CapacityReservationPreference [required], CapacityReservationTarget{CapacityReservationIds, CapacityReservationResourceGroupArns}} maps 1:1 to TF capacity_reservation_specification{capacity_reservation_preference, capacity_reservation_target{capacity_reservation_ids, capacity_reservation_resource_group_arns}} — clean (Cfn requires the preference; TF schema types it optional but AWS requires it).
- InstanceMaintenancePolicy{MaxHealthyPercentage, MinHealthyPercentage} (both Cfn-optional number, with a special "-1 to clear" sentinel) maps to TF instance_maintenance_policy{max_healthy_percentage, min_healthy_percentage} (both TF fields are *required* once the block is present — no "-1 to clear" sentinel; to clear in TF you omit/remove the whole block instead of setting -1).
- Durations are consistent in units (seconds) on both sides — no unit conversion for DefaultInstanceWarmup/default_instance_warmup, HealthCheckGracePeriod/health_check_grace_period, MaxInstanceLifetime/max_instance_lifetime, LifecycleHookSpecification.HeartbeatTimeout/heartbeat_timeout, Cooldown/default_cooldown. Caveat: Cfn's DefaultInstanceWarmup uses `-1` as a "clear the value" sentinel (Cfn-only convention) — no TF analogue, just omit the field in TF.
- AvailabilityZoneDistribution{CapacityDistributionStrategy} maps 1:1 to TF availability_zone_distribution{capacity_distribution_strategy} — clean.
- VPCZoneIdentifier (Cfn: Array<ISubnetRef|string>), LoadBalancerNames (Array<ILoadBalancerRef|string>), TargetGroupArns (Array<ITargetGroupRef|string>) map to plain TF string[] (vpc_zone_identifier, load_balancers, target_group_arns) — Cfn's typed L1 ref unions resolve to plain ARN/name strings in the emitted template, no functional shape difference for TF.
- Context (Cfn: "Reserved") maps directly to TF `context` (same semantics) despite Cfn docs marking it reserved.
- DesiredCapacityType maps directly to TF desired_capacity_type (both string enums units|vcpu|memory-mib) — clean.
- ServiceLinkedRoleArn (Cfn: iamRefs.IRoleRef | string) maps to TF service_linked_role_arn (plain string) — ref-resolves-to-string caveat.
- LaunchTemplateOverrides.WeightedCapacity is `string` on both Cfn and TF (override.weighted_capacity: string) — matches, no conversion needed.
- InstancesDistribution.OnDemandBaseCapacity/OnDemandPercentageAboveBaseCapacity/SpotInstancePools are `number` on both sides; SpotMaxPrice is `string` on both sides — clean parity.
- Confidence caveat: the aws_autoscaling_group provider-side schema also exposes waitForCapacityTimeout / waitForElbCapacity / minElbCapacity / ignoreFailedScalingActivities / forceDelete / forceDeleteWarmPool / namePrefix / suspendedProcesses / id / region / timeouts / instance_refresh block — none have a Cfn source (TF-only conveniences/behavior knobs), so leave at provider defaults during conversion.

tfResources.role: Primary 1:1 mapping. CfnLaunchConfiguration is a single flat resource and aws_launch_configuration (LaunchConfigurationConfig) is likewise a single flat resource — nearly all scalar props map directly (imageId->image_id, instanceType->instance_type, keyName->key_name, ebsOptimized->ebs_optimized, associatePublicIpAddress->associate_public_ip_address, iamInstanceProfile->iam_instance_profile, placementTenancy->placement_tenancy, securityGroups->security_groups, spotPrice->spot_price, userData->user_data/user_data_base64, launchConfigurationName->name or name_prefix). blockDeviceMappings (with nested BlockDeviceProperty) is re-shaped into three separate nested blocks on the TF side: ebs_block_device[], ephemeral_block_device[] and root_block_device (single). metadataOptions maps 1:1 (nested block, same field names/casing: httpEndpoint, httpPutResponseHopLimit, httpTokens) — this is the block read by require-imdsv2-aspect.ts. Verified against LaunchConfigurationConfig and the CfnLaunchConfigurationProps interface: no sub-resource splits are needed — warm pool, notification configurations, traffic-source attachments, MixedInstancesPolicy, instance-refresh and instance-maintenance-policy all belong to CfnAutoScalingGroup, not CfnLaunchConfiguration.

attributeNotes:
Cfn props with NO direct TF attribute on aws_launch_configuration (must be dropped/handled at synth time, e.g. warn+ignore in the terratitan launch-config construct):
- instanceId: TF has no "derive settings from an existing instance" mode; every field must be explicitly supplied (image_id/instance_type are required inputs). No equivalent — must error/require explicit values if instanceId-based CFN authoring is encountered.
- classicLinkVpcId / classicLinkVpcSecurityGroups: EC2-Classic is retired; aws_launch_configuration never had these fields. Drop with a deprecation warning.
- kernelId / ramDiskId: not exposed by aws_launch_configuration at all (AWS provider omits legacy PV-GRUB kernel/ramdisk fields for this resource, unlike aws_instance). No TF equivalent — must be dropped/warned.

Shape / casing / unit mismatches:
- blockDeviceMappings (flat array of {deviceName, ebs, noDevice, virtualName}) must be partitioned by the caller into three distinct TF constructs based on device semantics: entries with `ebs` and matching the AMI's root device name -> single `root_block_device` (TF's LaunchConfigurationRootBlockDevice exposes ONLY delete_on_termination/encrypted/iops/throughput/volume_size/volume_type — no device_name, no_device, or snapshot_id); entries with `ebs` for non-root devices -> `ebs_block_device[]` (keeps device_name, delete_on_termination, encrypted, iops, no_device, snapshot_id, throughput, volume_size, volume_type — all nine confirmed present); entries with `virtualName` (instance-store) -> `ephemeral_block_device[]` (device_name, no_device, virtual_name). CFN itself has no concept of a distinguished 'root' mapping — TF's split requires knowing/guessing which device_name is the AMI root device, a lossy/heuristic transform.
- userData: CFN's `userData` string is documented as already Base64-encoded (the CDK L1 expects a pre-encoded string, mirroring the raw CFN property). TF exposes two mutually exclusive fields: `user_data` (plain text — TF base64-encodes it for you) and `user_data_base64` (already-encoded, used verbatim). A CFN pre-encoded value should map to TF's `user_data_base64`, not `user_data`, to avoid double base64-encoding.
- launchConfigurationName: CFN has a single optional name (CFN auto-generates a physical name via provider-generated suffix if omitted). TF splits this into two mutually exclusive fields, `name` (exact name) and `name_prefix` (TF appends a random suffix) — construct authors typically use `name_prefix` to replicate CFN's auto-naming/replace-on-update behavior, since TF's `aws_launch_configuration` is immutable/create-before-destroy just like CFN's LC replacement semantics.
- instanceMonitoring (boolean, CFN default true) -> enable_monitoring (boolean, TF default true) — same semantics, only naming differs, no unit/shape mismatch.
- metadataOptions: no casing/shape mismatch — httpEndpoint, httpPutResponseHopLimit (number, both unitless PUT-response hop count 1-64), httpTokens ('optional'|'required') all line up field-for-field with the TF nested block (LaunchConfigurationMetadataOptions); this is the exact block the require-imdsv2-aspect.ts inspects/warns on for CDK token values.
- No MixedInstancesPolicy nesting applies here (that only exists on CfnAutoScalingGroup, not CfnLaunchConfiguration). Likewise instance-refresh and instance-maintenance-policy are CfnAutoScalingGroup concerns, not LC.
- arn is a TF-only computed attribute (get arn(): string getter on the class); CFN's launch configuration has no Fn::GetAtt attributes at all (only Ref returns the name) — so no corresponding Cfn attribute exists to lose, this is purely additive on the TF side.
- TF-only Config fields with no CFN counterpart: `id` (synthetic TF resource id) and `region` (per-resource provider region override / TerraformMetaArguments) — both are TF/provider plumbing, not lost CFN data.
- No AWS::AutoScaling::LaunchConfiguration Tags property exists (this CFN resource type does not support tags at all), so there is no tagging-related mismatch to reconcile against aws_launch_configuration (which likewise has no tags argument).

tfResources.role: Primary and sole mapping — direct 1:1 equivalent of the whole Cfn resource. Every Cfn prop maps to a TF attribute on this single resource; no other TF resources are needed.

attributeNotes:
Field-by-field mapping (CfnLifecycleHookProps -> AutoscalingLifecycleHookConfig, both flat/scalar, no nested blocks). Verified against autoscaling.generated.d.ts (lines 2268-2332) and autoscaling-lifecycle-hook/index.d.ts (lines 7-53):
- autoScalingGroupName (required, IAutoScalingGroupRef|string) -> autoscaling_group_name (required, string). Cfn allows a ref-object or string; TF takes a plain string (the ASG name/id), so a ref must be resolved to the group's `id`/`name` attribute.
- defaultResult (optional, string, CONTINUE|ABANDON, Cfn default ABANDON) -> default_result (optional, string). Enum values identical; straight passthrough.
- heartbeatTimeout (optional, number, seconds, 30-7200, Cfn default 3600) -> heartbeat_timeout (optional, number, seconds). Units and range identical, straight passthrough, no conversion.
- lifecycleHookName (optional in Cfn — CFN auto-generates a name if omitted) -> name (REQUIRED in TF, no default/auto-generation). Confirmed shape mismatch: TF `name` is a required string (index.d.ts line 34). If the Cfn template omits lifecycleHookName, the TF side must synthesize a name (e.g. `${stack}-hook` or random suffix) since TF has no equivalent auto-naming behavior.
- lifecycleTransition (required) -> lifecycle_transition (required). Identical string values (autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING / autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING).
- notificationMetadata (optional, string, opaque JSON payload) -> notification_metadata (optional, string). Both opaque strings; pass through as-is (neither side parses/validates).
- notificationTargetArn (optional, ITopicRef|IQueueRef|string) -> notification_target_arn (optional, string ARN). SNS Topic / SQS Queue ref objects must be resolved to their `.arn` attribute for TF.
- roleArn (optional, IRoleRef|string) -> role_arn (optional, string ARN). IAM role ref must resolve to `.arn`.
- TF-only attributes with no Cfn counterpart: `id` (optional/computed, import/state identifier — closest analog to Cfn Ref which returns the physical id == lifecycle hook name) and `region` (optional provider-level region override, handled at CDK stack/provider level, not per-resource).
- No Fn::GetAtt readonly attributes are exposed by CfnLifecycleHook beyond the standard Ref.
- Confirmed NO 1-to-many split: warm pool, notification configurations, traffic-source attachments, MixedInstancesPolicy, instance-refresh, and instance-maintenance-policy nesting belong to CfnAutoScalingGroup, NOT CfnLifecycleHook. This resource has zero nested blocks — it is one of the simplest Cfn->TF mappings in the autoscaling module.

tfResources.role: Primary and sole equivalent. Direct 1:1 mapping of every CfnScheduledActionProps field: autoScalingGroupName -> autoscaling_group_name, desiredCapacity -> desired_capacity, endTime -> end_time, maxSize -> max_size, minSize -> min_size, recurrence -> recurrence, startTime -> start_time, timeZone -> time_zone.

attributeNotes:
Verified attribute-by-attribute against autoscaling.generated.d.ts (CfnScheduledActionProps, lines 3429-3496) and @cdktn/provider-aws autoscaling-schedule/index.d.ts (AutoscalingScheduleConfig, lines 7-57). CfnScheduledActionProps has exactly 8 fields, all mapped 1:1 with no gaps:

- autoScalingGroupName (REQUIRED, typed `IAutoScalingGroupRef | string`) -> autoscaling_group_name (required string). When the Cfn prop is a ref, resolve to the underlying aws_autoscaling_group's `name` attribute.
- desiredCapacity? (number) -> desired_capacity? (number)
- endTime? (string, ISO-8601 UTC) -> end_time? (string)
- maxSize? (number) -> max_size? (number)
- minSize? (number) -> min_size? (number)
- recurrence? (string, 5-field cron, UTC by default) -> recurrence? (string)
- startTime? (string, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ UTC) -> start_time? (string)
- timeZone? (string, IANA tz name) -> time_zone? (string)

All string/number types line up directly; no unit, casing, or shape conversions needed.

TF-only fields (confirmed against index.d.ts):
- scheduled_action_name: REQUIRED input argument in TF, with NO corresponding Cfn input prop. In Cfn the action name is derived from the logical ID at deploy (attrScheduledActionName is a read-only @cloudformationAttribute returning the name, not an input). When generating TF config you MUST synthesize/derive a scheduled_action_name string (e.g. from the CDK construct id) since Cfn callers never supply it explicitly.
- arn: computed output attribute, no Cfn equivalent - drop or expose as output if downstream refs need it.
- region: optional provider-level regional override, not in Cfn - no action.
- id: SDKv2 provider artifact (optional/computed), no action.

No fan-out / one-to-many: CfnScheduledAction has NO nested or standalone-resource props. Warm pools (AWS::AutoScaling::WarmPool / CfnWarmPool), notification configurations, lifecycle hooks, traffic-source/target-group attachments, MixedInstancesPolicy, instance-refresh, and instance-maintenance-policy all belong to OTHER Cfn resources (CfnWarmPool, CfnAutoScalingGroup), not to CfnScheduledAction, so none of them are implicated here. This is a clean, complete 1:1 single-resource mapping.

cfnResource: AWS::AutoScaling::ScalingPolicy (CfnScalingPolicy, from aws-cdk-lib/aws-autoscaling; used internally by the StepScalingAction and TargetTrackingScalingPolicy L2 constructs in aws-autoscaling v2.233.0)

tfResources.role: Primary and effectively exclusive TF equivalent. AutoscalingPolicyConfig covers the entire CfnScalingPolicy surface: adjustment_type, autoscaling_group_name, cooldown, estimated_instance_warmup, metric_aggregation_type, min_adjustment_magnitude, name, policy_type, scaling_adjustment, plus nested blocks step_adjustment (repeatable), target_tracking_configuration, and predictive_scaling_configuration — all modeled as inline nested blocks/objects on the same TF resource rather than as separate top-level resources (unlike e.g. notifications or lifecycle hooks on the ASG side). None of the other candidates (autoscaling-group, autoscaling-lifecycle-hook, autoscaling-schedule, autoscaling-attachment, autoscaling-traffic-source-attachment, autoscaling-group-tag, autoscaling-notification, launch-template, launch-configuration) are relevant to CfnScalingPolicy. Verified: warm pool, notifications, traffic-source attachments, MixedInstancesPolicy, instance-refresh and instance-maintenance-policy all belong to AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup (CfnAutoScalingGroup), NOT to CfnScalingPolicy, so no 1-to-many split applies here — oneToMany is correctly false.

attributeNotes:
- attrArn (CFN output, @cloudformationAttribute Arn) -> TF computed attribute `arn` on AutoscalingPolicy: direct equivalent, both read-only/generated by the API.
- attrPolicyName (CFN output, @cloudformationAttribute PolicyName) has NO corresponding CFN input property — CloudFormation auto-generates the policy name and only exposes it as a Fn::GetAtt output. TF's `name` is instead a REQUIRED INPUT on AutoscalingPolicyConfig. Conversion must synthesize a deterministic name (e.g. from the CDK construct id / logical id) since CFN callers never supply one; there is no separate TF computed 'policyName' output beyond the input `name`.
- cooldown: CFN `cooldown` is typed as string (seconds, e.g. "300") while TF `cooldown` (AutoscalingPolicyConfig) is typed as number — same unit (seconds) but requires string->number coercion.
- TF adds `enabled` (boolean, default true), `region`, and `id` on AutoscalingPolicyConfig with no CFN equivalent property — CloudFormation ScalingPolicy has no enable/disable toggle, per-resource region override, or settable id; leave at TF default when converting from CFN.
- StepAdjustments: CFN `stepAdjustments` (array of StepAdjustmentProperty: metricIntervalLowerBound, metricIntervalUpperBound as number, scalingAdjustment as number) maps to TF `step_adjustment` block list (AutoscalingPolicyStepAdjustment), but TF's metric_interval_lower_bound / metric_interval_upper_bound are typed as STRING while CFN types them as number — numeric-to-string cast needed for both bound fields; scaling_adjustment stays number-to-number. Both sides: scalingAdjustment is required, the two bounds optional.
- TargetTrackingConfiguration: CFN TargetTrackingConfigurationProperty (targetValue, disableScaleIn, predefinedMetricSpecification, customizedMetricSpecification) maps cleanly to TF `target_tracking_configuration` block (AutoscalingPolicyTargetTrackingConfiguration) with matching sub-blocks predefined_metric_specification and customized_metric_specification — casing/shape is 1:1 (snake_case block vs PascalCase struct), no unit mismatches. targetValue required on both; disableScaleIn optional boolean on both. Both are single (max-1) objects, matching the CFN single-object shape.
- CustomizedMetricSpecification: CFN's structure supports EITHER the legacy single-metric form (metricName/namespace/statistic/unit/period/dimensions) OR the newer `metrics` (TargetTrackingMetricDataQuery[] with id/expression/label/metricStat/period/returnData -> metricStat.metric/period/stat/unit) math-expression form; TF's target_tracking_configuration.customized_metric_specification exposes the equivalent nested metric_dimension list and a `metrics` block list with the same fields (expression/id/label/return_data/metric_stat). The union-of-two-shapes nesting must be preserved and flattened into TF's blocks rather than assumed to be a single flat object. Note TF `metrics[].id` is required (as in CFN).
- PredictiveScalingConfiguration: CFN PredictiveScalingConfigurationProperty (maxCapacityBreachBehavior, maxCapacityBuffer, metricSpecifications array, mode, schedulingBufferTime) maps to TF `predictive_scaling_configuration` block (AutoscalingPolicyPredictiveScalingConfiguration) with a correspondingly deep nested chain (metric_specification -> customized_capacity/load/scaling_metric_specification -> metric_data_queries -> metric_stat -> metric -> dimensions), plus the predefined variants (predefined_load/predefined_metric_pair/predefined_scaling_metric_specification). CORRECTION to prior note: two TYPE mismatches exist here (units are unchanged but the scalar TYPE is not): CFN `maxCapacityBuffer` is number (percentage) while TF `max_capacity_buffer` is STRING, and CFN `schedulingBufferTime` is number (seconds) while TF `scheduling_buffer_time` is STRING — both need number->string coercion, analogous to cooldown/step-adjustment bounds. maxCapacityBreachBehavior and mode are string->string. CARDINALITY: CFN `metricSpecifications` is an ARRAY (max 1 supported by AWS) whereas TF `metric_specification` is a SINGLE (max-1) object block — the array's sole element must be unwrapped into the single TF block.
- PredictiveScaling deep nesting: CFN reuses generic MetricDataQueryProperty/MetricStatProperty/MetricProperty/MetricDimensionProperty across the customized capacity/load/scaling specs, while the TF provider generates DISTINCT, separately-named nested types for each of customized_capacity_metric_specification, customized_load_metric_specification, and customized_scaling_metric_specification (e.g. AutoscalingPolicyPredictiveScalingConfigurationMetricSpecificationCustomizedCapacityMetricSpecificationMetricDataQueriesMetricStatMetricDimensions) — conversion must duplicate/re-target the same logical metric-query shape into three parallel TF type paths rather than reference one shared type. Only structural re-nesting is required for these deep metric-query fields (no unit changes there); the scalar type coercions above are the only value conversions.
- autoScalingGroupName: CFN types this as `IAutoScalingGroupRef | string` (supports CDK's newer cross-stack resource-reference construct) while TF `autoscaling_group_name` is a plain required string — the ref form must be resolved to the group's name string during conversion.
- PolicyType, AdjustmentType, MetricAggregationType, MinAdjustmentMagnitude, ScalingAdjustment, EstimatedInstanceWarmup all map 1:1 by name/type (camelCase -> snake_case only) with no unit or shape conversion needed.

tfResources.role: primary — WarmPool has no standalone TF resource; it is expressed as the nested `warm_pool` block (AutoscalingGroupWarmPool) inside the aws_autoscaling_group resource that owns the group. The synthesizer must locate/merge into the referenced ASG's config rather than emit a separate resource.

attributeNotes:
VERIFIED against autoscaling.generated.d.ts (CfnWarmPoolProps lines 3595-3644, InstanceReusePolicyProperty lines 3579-3587) and @cdktn/provider-aws autoscaling-group/index.d.ts (AutoscalingGroupWarmPool line 1620, AutoscalingGroupWarmPoolInstanceReusePolicy line 1597, forceDeleteWarmPool line 47, warmPool line 210). The provider lib dir contains NO aws_autoscaling_warm_pool resource — confirmed by listing (only autoscaling-group, -attachment, -group-tag, -lifecycle-hook, -notification, -policy, -schedule, -traffic-source-attachment). Warm pool configuration is only the optional nested block `warm_pool { ... }` on aws_autoscaling_group. This is structural (1 Cfn resource -> 0 TF resources of its own, fields folded into an existing sibling resource) rather than 1:1.

Field-by-field:
- autoScalingGroupName (Cfn: IAutoScalingGroupRef | string, required) -> NO direct TF attribute on the warm_pool block; the whole warm_pool block must be attached to the aws_autoscaling_group construct corresponding to that ASG. Synthesizer must resolve the CfnWarmPool's autoScalingGroupName back to the owning AutoscalingGroup construct/resource and merge the block in-place (cannot be a sibling resource pointing by name/id the way Cfn does). Note the Cfn typing accepts either an IAutoScalingGroupRef (in-scope construct ref — resolvable/mergeable) or a plain string name (potentially external/imported).
- instanceReusePolicy (CfnWarmPool.InstanceReusePolicyProperty | IResolvable) -> warm_pool.instance_reuse_policy (AutoscalingGroupWarmPoolInstanceReusePolicy), a nested block. Casing: PascalCase Cfn HCL attr ReuseOnScaleIn -> snake_case reuse_on_scale_in in HCL; TS/JSII exposes camelCase reuseOnScaleIn in both Cfn and CDKTF typings, so no casing surprise at the L1 TS layer.
  - reuseOnScaleIn: boolean | IResolvable -> reuseOnScaleIn: boolean | cdktn.IResolvable — direct 1:1, no unit/shape mismatch. This is the ONLY field on InstanceReusePolicyProperty (both sides).
- maxGroupPreparedCapacity (number, optional; omit to let ASG default to max-desired difference, use -1 sentinel to explicitly clear a previously-set value) -> warm_pool.maxGroupPreparedCapacity (number) — direct 1:1.
- minSize (number, default 0) -> warm_pool.minSize (number) — direct 1:1.
- poolState (string enum: Stopped | Running | Hibernated, default Stopped) -> warm_pool.poolState (string) — direct 1:1, values pass through as literal strings, no casing/enum transform.

Additional TF-only knob with no Cfn counterpart: aws_autoscaling_group top-level `forceDeleteWarmPool` (boolean | IResolvable, index.d.ts line 47) controls destroy-time behavior; it lives on the ASG resource, not the warm_pool block, and should default to false/unset unless force-delete-on-destroy is wanted.

No Fn::GetAtt return values are defined for AWS::AutoScaling::WarmPool beyond implicit Ref (returns the ASG name). No separate TF computed 'warm pool id' attribute is needed since it isn't a distinct resource in TF state; the ASG resource's own id/name serves that purpose.

1-to-many check: notifications (AWS::AutoScaling::* notification config -> aws_autoscaling_notification), traffic source attachments (-> aws_autoscaling_traffic_source_attachment), lifecycle hooks, and scaling policies are SEPARATE Cfn resources, NOT sub-properties of CfnWarmPool, so no split applies to this mapping. CfnWarmPool has no MixedInstancesPolicy/instance-refresh/instance-maintenance-policy surface (those belong to the ASG/LaunchTemplate resources).

Synthesis implication: since TF collapses WarmPool into the ASG resource: (a) if the ASG is defined in the same app/scope (autoScalingGroupName given as IAutoScalingGroupRef, or a string resolvable to an in-scope construct), merge the warm_pool block into that AutoscalingGroup's TF config at synth time; (b) if the ASG is external/unknown (only a name string referencing an out-of-scope/imported group), there is no way to attach a nested block to an out-of-scope resource in TF — this case cannot be faithfully represented and should be flagged/rejected rather than silently dropped.
